news.titleTr: Fed üyesi Waller'dan sert faiz mesajı: Tahvil getirileri yükselişte
news.summaryTr: Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller, enflasyon görünümünün kötüleşmesi halinde aralık ayında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının gündeme gelebileceğini söyledi. Waller'ın açıklamalarının ardından ABD Hazine tahvillerinin getirileri yükselirken, piyasaların faiz artışı beklentileri güçlendi.
news.articleText: Fed üyesi Waller'dan sert faiz mesajı: Tahvil getirileri yükselişte - Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller, enflasyon görünümünün kötüleşmesi halinde aralık ayında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının gündeme gelebileceğini söyledi. Waller'ın açıklamalarının ardından ABD Hazine tahvillerinin getirileri yükselirken, piyasaların faiz artışı beklentileri güçlendi. ABD Merkez Bankası (Fed) Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller, para politikasının sıkılaştırılması konusunda beklemeye hazır olduğunu ancak daha önce taahhüt edilen faiz artışlarının makul bir süre içinde gerçekleştirilmesi gerektiğini belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Waller, ekim ayı enflasyon verilerinin eylül ayına göre iyileşme göstermesi halinde bile aralık ayında 25 baz puanlık faiz artışını destekleyeceğini ifade etti. Enflasyon görünümünün kötüleşmesi durumunda daha güçlü bir adım atılması gerektiğini vurgulayan Waller, ekim ayında aylık çekirdek tüketici fiyat endeksinin (TÜFE) yüzde 0,3 veya üzerinde artması halinde aralık toplantısında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. ABD ekonomisinde yavaşlama bekliyor ABD ekonomisinin mevcut çeyrekte yavaşladığını düşündüğünü belirten Waller, buna karşın ekonomik büyümenin güçlü bir hızda devam edeceğini öngördü. Fed yetkilisi, iş gücü piyasasının güçlü olduğunu, arz ve talebin büyük ölçüde dengelendiğini ve istihdamın Fed'in hedeflerine yakın seyrettiğini ifade etti. Fed uzmanlarının analizlerine de değinen Waller, üretici fiyatlarında daha fazla artış yaşanabileceğine ve enerji fiyatlarındaki şokun daha kalıcı olabileceğine işaret etti. news.title: ABD'den Hazar Denizi planı: İran ablukası genişliyor
news.summary: ABD'nin Merkez Kuvvetler Komutanlığı, 7 Kasım'da 20 kişilik "Demir Kapı" adlı askeri görev gücünü kurduğunu duyurdu. Planın uygulanmasında askeri gücün yanı sıra istihbarat, yaptırımlar, sınır denetimleri ve uluslararası işbirliğinin belirleyici olması bekleniyor.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: ABD'den Hazar Denizi planı: İran ablukası genişliyor
news.summaryTr: ABD'nin Merkez Kuvvetler Komutanlığı, 7 Kasım'da 20 kişilik "Demir Kapı" adlı askeri görev gücünü kurduğunu duyurdu. Planın uygulanmasında askeri gücün yanı sıra istihbarat, yaptırımlar, sınır denetimleri ve uluslararası işbirliğinin belirleyici olması bekleniyor.
news.articleText: ABD'den Hazar Denizi planı: İran ablukası genişliyor - ABD'nin, İran'a yönelik abluka planını Hürmüz Boğazı'nın ötesine taşıyarak kara sınırları ve Hazar Denizi'ni de kapsayacak şekilde genişletmeyi hedeflediği bildirildi. - ABD Merkez Kuvvetler Komutanlığı (CENTCOM), 7 Kasım'da "Demir Kapı" adını verdiği 20 kişilik askeri görev gücünün kurulduğunu açıkladı. - Planın başarıya ulaşmasının doğrudan askeri güç kullanımından çok istihbarat faaliyetleri, yaptırımların uygulanması, sınır denetimleri ve ülkeler arasındaki işbirliğine bağlı olduğu belirtiliyor. ABD'nin İran'a yönelik abluka planını genişleterek Hürmüz Boğazı'nın yanı sıra ülkenin kara sınırlarını ve Hazar Denizi'ni de kapsayacak şekilde uygulamayı hedeflediği bildirildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD, "Demir Kapı" adını verdiği girişimi duyurdu. ABD ile İsrail’in İran’a karşı başlattığı savaşın ardından Washington yönetimi, Tahran’ı yaptırımların yanı sıra "ablukayla" da baskı altına almaya çalışıyor. ABD ilk olarak yaptırımların yanı sıra 13 Nisan’da Hürmüz Boğazı çevresinde İran’a yönelik deniz ablukasını başlattı. Bu ablukayla ABD, İran’a giden veya bu ülkeden başka ülkelere gönderilen gemilerin geçişini engelliyor. Pakistan aracılığıyla haziran ayında varılan mutabakatın uygulanamaması nedeniyle ABD, ekonomik baskıyı artırmak için şimdi de İran'ı karadan ve Hazar Denizi’nden ablukaya almak için yeni bir girişim duyurdu. ABD'nin Merkez Kuvvetler Komutanlığı (CENTCOM), 7 Kasım'da da "Demir Kapı" adını verdiği askeri görev gücünün kurulduğunu açıkladı. CENTCOM'un açıklamasına göre, ABD'nin Florida eyaletinin Tampa kentindeki hava üssünde konuşlandırılacak görev gücü, İran'ın kara sınırları ve Hazar Denizi üzerinden gerçekleştirdiği silah sevkiyatını, hem sivil hem de askeri alanlarda kullanılan teknoloji transferini, ABD'nin tek taraflı yaptırımlarına tabi malzeme sevkiyatını ve "yasa dışı" gelir hareketlerini engellemek amacıyla diğer ABD kurumlarıyla koordinasyon sağlayacak. Bu girişim, yaklaşık 20 kişilik bir CENTCOM görev gücünden oluşuyor. "Demir Kapı" adı verilen girişim, İran'ın sınırlarını fiziksel olarak kapatabilecek bir askeri kuvvet değil. Dolayısıyla uzmanlar, projenin başarısının doğrudan askeri güçten ziyade istihbarat, yaptırım uygulamaları, sınır denetimi ve ülkeler arası işbirliğine bağlı olduğunu belirtiyor. Başarı şansı var mı? ABD’nin "Demir Kapı" ile ablukayı ağırlaştırmayı amaçladığı İran’ın; Türkiye, Azerbaycan, Türkmenistan, Pakistan, Irak, Ermenistan ve Afganistan olmak üzere 7 ülkeyle kara sınırı bulunuyor. Buna ek olarak Tahran’a yaptırımlara karşı çıkan Rusya’nın Hazar Denizi üzerinden İran’la bağlantısı bulunuyor. Uzmanlara göre, "Demir Kapı" girişiminin İran’a yönelik kara ablukasının başarı şansı oldukça düşük. Zira, ABD'nin bazı ülkelerle sınırındaki geçişlere yönelik denetimleri artırması halinde ticaretin diğer güzergahlara kaymasına imkan tanıyabilir. Özellikle komşu ülkelerin İran'la ekonomik ilişkilerini sürdürme konusundaki tutumlarının, bu alternatif kanalların kullanılabilirliğini doğrudan etkilediği ifade ediliyor. Ayrıca kara yolu ve demir yolu bağlantılarının farklı ülkelere uzanmasının ticaretin tek bir sınır hattına bağımlı kalmasını önlediği kaydediliyor. Buna ek olarak Rusya ve Çin’in ABD yaptırımlarına karşı çıkması ve uygulamaması da ablukanın uygulanabilirliğini düşürüyor. Moskova ve Pekin'in ABD'nin yaptırım politikalarını büyük oranda benimsememesi ve Tahran ile ekonomik ilişkilerini korumasının, Washington'ın denetim mekanizmalarının kapsamını sınırlayabileceği de değerlendiriliyor. Hazar ülkelerinin işbirliği kritik olacak Hazar Denizi de projenin uygulama kapasitesini etkileyen önemli bir alan olarak öne çıkıyor. Rusya, İran, Azerbaycan, Kazakistan ve Türkmenistan'ın kıyıdaş olduğu bölgede ABD'nin deniz denetimi bulunmuyor. Bu nedenle Hazar üzerinden İran'ın gerçekleştirdiği ticaretin sınırlandırılması da bu ülkelerin ABD ile bu konuda işbirliğine bağlı. Son olarak, kara ve demir yolu taşımacılığının farklı ülkelerin egemenlik alanlarından geçmesi, ABD'nin doğrudan müdahale kapasitesini sınırlandırıyor. Gümrük işlemleri, transit geçişler ve sınır denetimleri ilgili ülkelerin yetkisinde bulunuyor. Bölge ülkelerinin İran'la ilişkileri ve ABD yaptırımlarına yaklaşımları arasındaki farklılıklar da ortak bir denetim mekanizması oluşturulmasını güçleştiriyor. Bu koşullar altında ABD'nin belirli sevkiyatları engellemesi, tedarik maliyetlerini artırması ve bazı ticaret ağlarını dağıtması mümkün olsa da İran'ın bütün alternatif ticaret güzergahlarını ve askeri tedarik bağlantılarını kesmesi çok daha kapsamlı uluslararası işbirliği gerektiriyor. İran'ın ticaret kanallarının tamamen kesilmesi durumunda ise Tahran'ın Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki deniz trafiği üzerindeki baskıyı artırması ve Körfez'deki enerji altyapısına yönelik tehditlerini hayata geçirmesi, bölgesel gerilimin daha da tırmanmasına yol açabilecek muhtemel karşılıklar arasında değerlendiriliyor.

news.title: Fed'in aralık kararı için kritik veri: Bankalardan enflasyon tahminleri
news.summary: ABD'de bugün açıklanacak ekim ayı enflasyonu öncesinde küresel bankaların tahminleri yüzde 0,2 ile yüzde 0,5 arasında değişiyor.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Fed'in aralık kararı için kritik veri: Bankalardan enflasyon tahminleri
news.summaryTr: ABD'de bugün açıklanacak ekim ayı enflasyonu öncesinde küresel bankaların tahminleri yüzde 0,2 ile yüzde 0,5 arasında değişiyor.
news.articleText: Fed'in aralık kararı için kritik veri: Bankalardan enflasyon tahminleri ABD'de bugün açıklanacak ekim ayı enflasyonu öncesinde küresel bankaların tahminleri yüzde 0,2 ile yüzde 0,5 arasında değişiyor. ABD'de piyasaların odağında ekim ayı tüketici enflasyonu verileri bulunuyor. ABD Çalışma İstatistikleri Bürosu (BLS), ekim ayına ilişkin tüketici fiyat endeksi (TÜFE) verilerini bugün TSİ 16.30'da açıklayacak. Dow Jones anketine göre tüketici fiyatlarının aylık yüzde 0,3, gıda ve enerji fiyatlarını dışlayan çekirdek TÜFE'nin ise yüzde 0,2 artması bekleniyor. Eylülde manşet enflasyon yüzde 0,6, çekirdek enflasyon yüzde 0,3 yükselmişti. Bankaların tahminleri yüzde 0,2 ile yüzde 0,5 arasında Küresel bankaların ekim ayı manşet enflasyon tahminleri birbirinden ayrışıyor. Citi, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, HSBC ve Morgan Stanley'nin de aralarında bulunduğu 10 kurum aylık yüzde 0,2 artış bekliyor. JPMorgan, UBS, BNP Paribas, Wells Fargo ve ING'nin de yer aldığı 18 kurumun tahmini yüzde 0,3 seviyesinde bulunuyor. SEB, U.S. Bank ve Westpac yüzde 0,4 artış öngörürken, Sparta Capital yüzde 0,5 ile en yüksek tahmini paylaşıyor. Bank of America: "Aralıkta faiz artışı büyük ölçüde kesinleşebilir" Bank of America ekonomisti Stephen Juneau, ekim enflasyonunun Fed'in 8-9 Aralık toplantısı öncesindeki son enflasyon raporu olacağına dikkat çekti. Juneau, banka tahminlerinin gerçekleşmesi halinde Fed'in 25 baz puanlık yeni bir faiz artışına gitmesinin büyük ölçüde kesinleşebileceğini belirtti. Aylık enflasyonda yüzde 0,1 gibi belirgin biçimde zayıf bir artış görülmediği sürece verilerin Fed'i faiz artışından vazgeçirmesini beklemediklerini ifade etti. Banka, faiz kararı açısından finansal piyasalardaki gelişmelerin de belirleyici olabileceğini değerlendiriyor. Hisse senedi piyasalarında sert bir satış dalgası yaşanması, faiz artışı beklentisini etkileyebilecek riskler arasında gösteriliyor. news.titleTr: Bitcoin price eyes $74K as Fed rate-hike bets hit 96% after Waller speech
news.summaryTr: Bitcoin price action and stock futures trended lower after Fed governor Christopher Waller said that he would vote to raise interest rates by 0.25% at the December FOMC meeting.
news.articleText: Bitcoin price eyes $74K as Fed rate-hike bets hit 96% after Waller speech Bitcoin price action and stock futures trended lower after Fed governor Christopher Waller said that he would vote to raise interest rates by 0.25% at the December FOMC meeting. Bitcoin (BTC) fell toward $74,000, and US stock futures dropped on Tuesday as a senior Federal Reserve official voiced support for hiking interest rates. Key points: - Bitcoin traded 1.3% lower on Tuesday, reaching $74,080 as Nasdaq futures fell 0.4% ahead of the Wall Street open. - October US CPI data, due for release at 8.30am on Tuesday, is expected to show a monthly increase of 0.3%, less than September’s 0.6% gain. - Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said that he would “support” a 0.25% interest-rate hike at the Dec. 9 FOMC meeting regardless of Tuesday’s CPI reading. Waller would “still support” December rate hike after lower CPI Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD reaching $74,080 on Bitstamp, down 1.3% on the day. BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView US stock market futures leaned lower as Fed governor Christopher Waller said that he would support hiking interest rates by 25 basis points at the next meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Dec. 9. At the time of writing, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.4%. His decision, he added, would not be swayed by lower-than-expected inflation data. The October prints of the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) is due for release at 8.30 am Eastern time on Tuesday. It is expected to show a month-on-month increase of 0.3% versus September when the increase was 0.6%, pushed higher by rising fuel costs. “While I am hoping for an improvement over September, even if this occurs, I would still support a 25 basis point increase in the FOMC’s policy rate at our December meeting,” Waller commented in a speech at the Bank of England Watchers Conference in London. “However, if inflation comes in substantially higher than I expect, more robust action by the FOMC may be called for.” US CPI 12-month % change. Source: BLS While CPI is particularly sensitive to fuel-price volatility, Waller also flagged high readings from the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, known to be the Fed’s “preferred” inflation gauge and which he confirmed was the “measure targeted by the FOMC.” “Let’s just say it. September’s inflation data were bad. There was no silver lining,” he said, referring to PCE rising 0.5% month-on-month and 3.7% year-on-year, respectively. Following the speech, markets immediately repriced odds of a 25-basis-point hike in December from 76.3% to 96.3%, per data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. Fed target-rate probability comparison for December FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group 2025 government shutdown to limit market CPI cues Financial policy tightening measures traditionally act as headwinds for crypto and risk asset prices as they imply a reduction in liquidity and associated capital inflows. Related: Bitcoin, tech stocks brush off Nvidia nerves as analyst mulls $68K target Commenting on the impetus for the expected slowdown in CPI upside for October, Christopher Hodge, chief US economist at Natixis CIB Americas, pointed to price declines in both fuel and shelter. “We think the slowdown in core CPI will stem from a reversion of shelter prices, primarily owners’ equivalent rents and lodging away from home. Similarly, the stabilization in diesel prices should help to quell price pressures in energy-intensive goods,” he wrote, quoted by CNBC. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), which publishes CPI, confirmed that Tuesday’s release would include only month-on-month statistics due to the 2025 US government shutdown reducing data availability. CPI data for October 2025 was not issued for the same reason.

news.titleTr: Bakan Şimşek'den güçlü sanayi vurgusu: "Dirençli seyir sürüyor"
news.summaryTr: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, sanayi üretiminin eylülde aylık yüzde 2,1, yıllık yüzde 2,6 arttığını belirterek, küresel ekonomideki belirsizliklere rağmen üretimde dirençli seyrin sürdüğünü ifade etti.
news.articleText: Bakan Şimşek'den güçlü sanayi vurgusu: "Dirençli seyir sürüyor" - Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, sanayi üretiminin eylülde aylık yüzde 2,1, yıllık yüzde 2,6 arttığını vurgulayarak, küresel ekonomideki belirsizliklere rağmen üretimde dirençli seyrin sürdüğünü ifade etti. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, sanayi üretiminde küresel ekonomideki belirsizliklere rağmen dirençli seyrin devam ettiğini belirtti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakan Şimşek, eylül ayına ilişkin sanayi üretim verilerini değerlendirdi. Şimşek, X sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı değerlendirmede, sanayi üretiminin eylül ayında aylık yüzde 2,1, yıllık yüzde 2,6 arttığını hatırlattı. Yüksek teknoloji üretiminin ocak-eylül döneminde yıllık yüzde 7,6 yükseldiğini kaydeden Şimşek, bu artışın katma değer ve verimlilik odaklı politikaların sonuçlarını yansıttığını ifade etti. Küresel ekonomide belirsizliklerin öne çıktığı 2026 yılında sanayi üretiminde dirençli seyir sürüyor. Üretim eylülde aylık yüzde 2,1, yıllık yüzde 2,6 arttı. Ocak-Eylül döneminde yıllık yüzde 7,6 artan yüksek teknoloji üretimi, katma değer ve verimlilik odaklı politikalarımızın sonuçlarını yansıtıyor. 2026 yılında ticaret ortaklarımızdaki zayıf talebe rağmen ekonomimizde ılımlı büyüme devam ederken küresel talebin ve finansal koşulların iyileşmesiyle önümüzdeki dönemde üretimdeki görünümün güçlenmesini bekliyoruz. Sanayide üretim kapasitesini, katma değeri ve verimliliği artıracak desteklerimize ve yapısal dönüşüm adımlarımıza devam edeceğiz. — Mehmet Simsek (@memetsimsek) November 10, 2026 Üretimde güçlenme beklentisi 2026 yılında ticaret ortaklarındaki zayıf talebe rağmen Türkiye ekonomisinde ılımlı büyümenin devam ettiğini belirten Şimşek, küresel talebin ve finansal koşulların iyileşmesiyle önümüzdeki dönemde üretim görünümünün güçlenmesini beklediklerini bildirdi. Şimşek, sanayide üretim kapasitesini, katma değeri ve verimliliği artıracak desteklere ve yapısal dönüşüm adımlarına devam edeceklerini kaydetti.

news.articleText: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash - Published Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering customers refunds for its $148 (£110) advent calendar which has been widely criticised on social media. The accessories advent calendar promised "twelve days of fun surprises" but has been mocked online for the quality of its contents, such as hair clips and keychains, with some comparing them to something you would find down the back of a sofa. A spokesperson for Skims has told a number of media outlets "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations" and the company has "personally contacted every customer" to offer a full refund or credit to put towards other products". The BBC has contacted Skims for comment. The shapewear and clothing business was co-founder by Kardashian in 2019 and has made the reality TV star a billionaire, according to Forbes magazine. Skims was valued at $5bn in 2025 when it raised millions of dollars in new funding. One account on TikTok called spicychathouse compared the contents of the calendar to things "my cat collects from around my house". Another account said it looked like "a bunch of stuff that Kim Kardashian was emptying out of her bedside table". A number of accounts showed people cleaning out their own sofas and claiming they had accidentally created the Skims advent calendar. What's in the Skim's advent calendar? news.summary: Households dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax will benefit.

news.titleTr: Thousands of 'off-grid' homes eligible for £250 to help with heating bills
news.summaryTr: Households dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax will benefit.
news.articleText: Thousands of 'off-grid' homes eligible for £250 to help with heating bills - Published Up to 20,000 homes using heating oil could get a £250 payment from the Welsh government to help with the rising cost of living. The government said £5m from a new £130m package will help "off grid" households who are dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax. The package includes the £100 household energy payment, with this extended to those eligible for council tax relief "irrespective of band". It also includes £7m support for bus travel and £8m for councils to help those "not captured by other schemes". It follows the UK government unveiling a £100 "household energy payment" for council taxpayers in bands A-D in England in October. Wales' Deputy First Minister Sioned Williams said supporting families with the cost of living was a "key priority". "We understand that this is a challenging time for many households across Wales," she said. "In total this represents an additional investment of £130m, providing immediate relief for households this winter. While we are taking firm action wherever we can, we need the UK Government to play its part". Five million pounds of the package will help towards "off-grid" fuel costs with a £250 payment available to households eligible for Council Tax Reduction based on their incomes and are dependent on either heating oil or LPG. An additional £8m will allow councils to extend the £100 payment to households "not captured" by other schemes and are facing financial hardship. While £7m is being made available to support bus operators with their high fuel costs and protect passengers from fares increases. The Welsh government said with winter approaching and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, "the coming months will be a challenging time for many". "This package represents a significant investment in Welsh communities and reflects our determination to stand alongside households during challenging times," it added. The Welsh government had already said it would make the £100 energy payment to about one million households in Wales following Chancellor John Healey's UK Budget announcement in October. The chancellor said council taxpayers in bands A-D in England would get the payment and urged the Welsh government to follow his lead, with Wales' Finance Minister Elin Jones subsequently saying households in the same bands in Wales would also benefit. Healey announced an end to gas standing charges but did not address call to help those people, mainly in rural areas, who relied on either heating oil or LPG. news.articleTextTr: Thousands of 'off-grid' homes eligible for £250 to help with heating bills - Published Up to 20,000 homes using heating oil could get a £250 payment from the Welsh government to help with the rising cost of living. The government said £5m from a new £130m package will help "off grid" households who are dependent on either heating oil or LPG and are eligible for reduced council tax. The package includes the £100 household energy payment, with this extended to those eligible for council tax relief "irrespective of band". It also includes £7m support for bus travel and £8m for councils to help those "not captured by other schemes". It follows the UK government unveiling a £100 "household energy payment" for council taxpayers in bands A-D in England in October. Wales' Deputy First Minister Sioned Williams said supporting families with the cost of living was a "key priority". "We understand that this is a challenging time for many households across Wales," she said. "In total this represents an additional investment of £130m, providing immediate relief for households this winter. While we are taking firm action wherever we can, we need the UK Government to play its part". Five million pounds of the package will help towards "off-grid" fuel costs with a £250 payment available to households eligible for Council Tax Reduction based on their incomes and are dependent on either heating oil or LPG. An additional £8m will allow councils to extend the £100 payment to households "not captured" by other schemes and are facing financial hardship. While £7m is being made available to support bus operators with their high fuel costs and protect passengers from fares increases. The Welsh government said with winter approaching and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, "the coming months will be a challenging time for many". news.articleText: Emlak Katılım'dan KAP açıklaması: Katılımevim ve Birevim devirlerine onay çıktı - Türkiye Emlak Katılım Bankası, Katılımevim, Birevim ve İktisat Katılım'ın pay devir işlemleri için Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı, Rekabet Kurumu, SPK ve BDDK nezdindeki izin ve onay süreçlerinin tamamlandığını duyurdu. Türkiye Emlak Katılım Bankası, Katılımevim Tasarruf Finansman A.Ş., Birevim Tasarruf Finansman A.Ş. ve İktisat Katılım Bankası A.Ş.'nin pay devir işlemlerine ilişkin gerekli izin ve onayların alındığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bankanın Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladığı açıklamaya göre, pay devir işlemleri kapsamında T.C. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Kamu Sermayeli Kuruluş ve İşletmeler Genel Müdürlüğü, Rekabet Kurumu, Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) ve Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu (BDDK) nezdinde yürütülen süreçler tamamlandı. Açıklamada, ilgili mevzuat uyarınca pay devir işlemleri için gerekli izin ve onayların alındığı bildirildi. Türkiye Emlak Katılım Bankası, konuya ilişkin daha önce 17, 25 ve 30 Eylül 2026 tarihlerinde de KAP üzerinden açıklamalarda bulunmuştu.

news.title: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
news.summary: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation change.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
news.summaryTr: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation change.
news.articleText: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely' - Published Donald Trump has said "Iran militarily is effectively over", and said that there is "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the Middle East conflict. "We're just keeping it the status quo," the US president said on Monday. "And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours." Trump's comments came after he met the Qatari prime minister. Qatar is a US ally in the Gulf region, and one of Iran's neighbours, which has been a key mediator in efforts to end the war. Addressing reporters in the White House press briefing room, Trump said that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" but that the US was "locked and loaded" should the circumstances change. Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed doubts about Trump's prior comments about resolving the conflict. This is not the first time that Trump has said the Iran war is "militarily" over, but the circumstances for him are different now. The president has hinted at de-escalation in Iran after a bruising set of midterm election results for the Republicans last week, which senior figures including Vice-President JD Vance blamed on the Iran war. Ahead of the midterms, Trump had said US forces conducted what he described as "minor strikes" on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz. However, in an interview with 60 Minutes that aired on Sunday, the president said that he did not currently see "any reason" to escalate the conflict. Responding to a question over why he would not officially declare an end to the war, Trump said that some of the Gulf allies could still face Iranian aggression. "We have some great allies there and we have to make sure they're not hurt," he said, suggesting that the US naval blockade on Iranian ports was helping to make the region more secure. Global oil prices, which have fallen sharply since the midterms, dipped further after Trump's comments. On Tuesday afternoon in Asia, Brent crude was more than 1% lower at $91.50 (£52) while US-traded was down by 1.2% at $85.82. Trump hosted Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani in the Oval Office earlier on Monday, saying they had an "excellent conversation" about negotiations to end the war. In a post on X, the Qatari leader said he held "positive discussions" with Trump and Vance on "reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region". Efforts to broker a peace between Washington and Tehran have largely been held indirectly through mediators since the war first broke out following joint US-Israeli strikes in February. Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are among the US's Gulf allies that have been hit by Iranian strikes over the course of the war, in addition to the threat of strikes that have led to major air travel disruptions in the region. Post-election recriminations over the US war in Iran are already placing pressure on members of the Trump administration. Republican congressman Thomas Massie launched a strong attack against Trump's Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over the war in Iran, requesting a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach him. Trump has backed Hegseth, who says he is "not worried" about the looming impeachment threats, calling Massie's effort a "sham". While the move is unlikely to succeed with Republicans still in control of Congress until January, Democrats have expressed willingness to impeach Hegseth once the new session begins and they have control of both the House and the Senate. - Published9 hours ago - Published2 days ago

news.articleText: Bitcoin yatırımcısına kritik uyarı: 73 bin 500 doların altına dikkat! - CoinTR CEO'su Ali Eşelioğlu, kripto para piyasasında satış baskısının sürdüğünü belirterek Bitcoin'de 73 bin 500 dolar seviyesine dikkat çekti. - Eşelioğlu, bu seviyenin aşağı yönlü kırılması halinde 68 bin dolara kadar geri çekilme yaşanabileceğini söyledi. CoinTR CEO'su Ali Eşelioğlu, CNBC-e canlı yayınında kripto para piyasalarındaki son gelişmeleri değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Piyasada satış baskısının etkili olduğunu belirten Eşelioğlu, geçen hafta yaşanan siber saldırının yatırımcı güvenini olumsuz etkilediğini ifade etti. Bitcoin ETF'lerinde eylül ayından bu yana ilk kez tek haftada bu ölçekte satış gerçekleştiğini söyleyen Eşelioğlu, Ethereum tarafında da güçlü satışlar görüldüğünü kaydetti. ABD'de Demokratların çoğunluğu sağlamasıyla gündeme gelen regülasyon adımlarının da piyasalar üzerinde negatif etki yaratabileceğini belirten Eşelioğlu, kripto varlıklara yeni para girişinin sınırlı kaldığına dikkat çekti. Bitcoin'de 73 bin 500 dolar kritik seviye Bitcoin'in 73 bin 500-76 bin 200 dolar aralığında hareket ettiğini belirten Eşelioğlu, bu bölgenin korunmasının önemli olduğunu vurguladı. Bitcoin'in mevcut seviyelerde tutunması halinde 78 bin ve 83 bin dolar seviyelerinin yeniden gündeme gelebileceğini ifade eden Eşelioğlu, 73 bin 500 doların altına inilmesi durumunda ise 68 bin dolara kadar geri çekilme ihtimalinin bulunduğunu söyledi. Bitcoin ETF'leri, yatırımcıların doğrudan kripto para satın almadan Bitcoin fiyat hareketlerine yatırım yapmasına imkan tanıyor. Bu fonlardaki para giriş ve çıkışları, kurumsal yatırımcıların piyasa eğilimini izlemek açısından önem taşıyor.

news.title: Holiday hunger bill to face final Stormont hurdle
news.summary: The new law would would help poorer families with food costs during school holidays.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Holiday hunger bill to face final Stormont hurdle
news.summaryTr: The new law would would help poorer families with food costs during school holidays.
news.articleText: Holiday hunger bill to face final Stormont hurdle - Published A proposed law which would help poorer families with food costs during school holidays is to face its final hurdle in the Northern Ireland Assembly on Tuesday. Some parents and charities have welcomed the Holiday Meal Payments Bill, external, which was brought forward by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker. It would create a new payment for families whose children receive free school meals, which would be made outside of term time to help with the cost of food. But Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) Education Minister Paul Givan has been consistently critical of the legislation, warning it will immediately cost his budget £25m to £30m a year at a time when all departments are struggling financially. Why was the bill introduced? Baker said he was motivated to introduce it by some of his experiences of breakfast clubs and meal schemes in youth work. "There was a young boy, about the same age of my youngest, around seven years old," he explained. "He was filling his wee pockets up and we caught on to this. "To cut a long story short, he was bringing home food for his siblings because there just wasn't enough food in the house." Baker said all ministers had choices to make and the legislation alone could not solve child poverty, but would act as an "early intervention". Children are eligible for free school meals if their family's household income is below £15,390 a year. Northern Ireland is the only UK region without government-funded holiday food support, after the Department of Education (DE) ended its £27-per-fortnight holiday meal grant in 2023. Baker's legislation was introduced in the Northern Ireland Assembly in March and has been scrutinised by members of the legislative assembly (MLAs) on a number of occasions over the past nine months. What have campaigners and charities said? Community and voluntary groups have been publicly supportive of the bill, with some staging a demonstration at Stormont on Monday in a bid to urge MLAs to get it over the finish line. Louise McCullough, a mum-of-three from east Belfast, was among those who spoke at the event. She said her children receive free school meals and that she would be directly affected by the legislation. "There are so many working families who need this, it will change their lives and be massively impactful," she told BBC News NI. "I can't afford to work full time because of the cost of childcare, and the cost of living. "We have to do what we can and schemes like free school meals make a difference but so much more needs done... if you can't find money for hungry children what are you doing? "Our government should be scaffolding our families properly." Edel Diamond from the South West Belfast Foodbank said organisations like hers had been "filling in the gaps" to help struggling families. "We shouldn't have to - it's incumbent on our executive to put these initiatives forward," she said. "This will make such a difference to families we're seeing daily." What is the education minister's view? Paul Givan said his department does not have enough money to cover meal costs outside of school terms. Speaking to the BBC's Good Morning Ulster programme ahead of the vote, he warned other education services would have to be cut to fund meal payments. "The problem with [Baker's] private member's bill is that this funding doesn't come from the Department of Finance," Givan said. "It is a Sinn Féin private member's bill with a Sinn Féin finance minister that are literally picking the pocket of the Department for Education to pay a welfare payment." He warned it will "require an annual commitment of nearly £25m to £30m" and challenged supporters to identify which services they would cut to pay for it. "To take the funding out of special educational needs and maintenance programmes in schools in order to make a welfare payment to people that are entitled to free school meals is not a responsible decision," Givan added. Last month, his department tabled amendments that would have given him power to delay its implementation, but these were rejected by a majority of parties. Ulster Unionist leader Jon Burrows said his party would not support the bill, saying that it was "undermining" the executive's case for asking London for additional funding to solve its budget impasse. Although the DUP and UUP are set to vote against the bill on Tuesday, Sinn Féin is expected to have enough support from Alliance and SDLP MLAs to ensure the bill passes. - Published30 March 2023 - Published12 October

"It is a Sinn Féin private member's bill with a Sinn Féin finance minister that are literally picking the pocket of the Department for Education to pay a welfare payment." He warned it will "require an annual commitment of nearly £25m to £30m" and challenged supporters to identify which services they would cut to pay for it. "To take the funding out of special educational needs and maintenance programmes in schools in order to make a welfare payment to people that are entitled to free school meals is not a responsible decision," Givan added. Last month, his department tabled amendments that would have given him power to delay its implementation, but these were rejected by a majority of parties. Ulster Unionist leader Jon Burrows said his party would not support the bill, saying that it was "undermining" the executive's case for asking London for additional funding to solve its budget impasse. Although the DUP and UUP are set to vote against the bill on Tuesday, Sinn Féin is expected to have enough support from Alliance and SDLP MLAs to ensure the bill passes. - Published30 March 2023 - Published12 October

news.summary: Huang, who is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, is far more important to the future of the world order than other tech bosses.

news.titleTr: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security
news.summaryTr: Huang, who is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, is far more important to the future of the world order than other tech bosses.
news.articleText: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security - Published Jensen Huang has the air of the late Steve Jobs about him. I have interviewed both, and the up-close charisma - and occasionally scratchy genius - is shared. Both sported a signature item of black clothing, although Huang opts for a leather jacket rather than the Apple founder's turtle neck. Both are innovators revered in the tech world. However, Huang is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Everything you have heard about Artificial Intelligence (AI) over the past few months - good, bad, revolutionary and catastrophic - is dependent on having the most powerful frontier AI models. In turn they depend on the most powerful microchips, and for years that has been this very company, Nvidia, led by Huang, and his technology rooted in repurposed games graphics and the manufacturing prowess of Taiwan. Names such as Gracehopper, Vera and Rubin mean almost nothing to the public, but are the names of chips powering the creation of AI models transforming the world. I met Huang as he held court with reporters and offered words of encouragement for the UK's tech future during US President Donald Trump's state visit to the UK in September last year. It was also right in the middle of his attempts to get Trump to lift export bans to China of some of the highest performing AI chips, specifically the H200. An export ban on a less powerful chip had already been lifted. He was, I suggested to him, one of the few people who could walk into the White House to meet Trump, and a few days later meet President Xi Jinping in Beijing. He made no secret of his views, nor his assessment that he had persuaded Trump of his case. "President Trump is very clear. He wants America to win and and President Xi wants China to win, and it's possible for both of them too. And the reason for that is because it's not a zero-sum game. The advance of human society is not a zero-sum game." He is probably the only person in the world that could have spoken that sentence with the authority that he might have heard personally from both these superpower leaders. Differing views on security risks However, his view about "zero-sum game" is not backed by many in national security circles. Their view is that the race to the most advanced forms of AI is entirely zero sum, and requires the West - and the US in particular - to take critical action to hold back Chinese advancement. The country that creates the most powerful AI systems, from the most powerful chips, will win, in terms of scientific development, of cracking encryption, economic growth and cyber-weapons. He made a further argument: Far from being a national security challenge, it was, in fact, better for the US that the world "including China" became dependent on US systems, what they called the "American tech stack", with Nvidia chips at its core. Huang then went even further than that, saying that President Trump "is very clear-eyed" about the idea that "this computing technology is not a national security concern". He told me "any military is smart enough to build their military on top of their own indigenous technology, and not rely on an adversary to build their technology, build their military capability". What does this show us? At that time, which is the same moment now being independently investigated over national security concerns and alleged Chinese espionage, Huang was making clear public arguments to lift export bans, and seemed to have a clear idea of President Trump's views. More than that, he was also disputing the idea that his technology, in China's hands, was any type of national security concern. Nvidia is the absolute epicentre of the AI tech boom in the US and of the global race for AI supremacy. Even if the boom turned to bust, Nvidia is still expected to remain in rude health. It has actual hard revenues of about $400bn this year. Monday's drop of about 4% of its value reflects new and extraordinary risks at this junction of tech and global politics, but the chipmaker is still worth more than $4 trillion. - Published2 hours ago - Published15 hours ago - Published11 hours ago

news.title: Headteachers say families will struggle after another rise in school dinner prices
news.summary: The price of a school dinner in a primary school will have risen from £2.60 to £3.40 since the start of 2026.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Headteachers say families will struggle after another rise in school dinner prices
news.summaryTr: The price of a school dinner in a primary school will have risen from £2.60 to £3.40 since the start of 2026.
news.articleText: Headteachers say families will struggle after another rise in school dinner prices - Published A headteacher has said she believes "families are going to struggle" as the price of school dinners is to increase for the second year in a row. The price of meals for pre-school, primary and special school pupils will go up by 30p, for post-primary pupils will they will rise by 15%. It follows an increase of just under 20% introduced by the Education Authority (EA) in January 2026. Áine Leslie, principal of Malone Integrated College in Belfast, said this will put further pressure on families who are already worried about the cost of living crisis. But the EA said that the amount parents would have to pay was still well below the average cost of producing a school meal, estimated at over £5.20. How much do school dinners cost in NI? The latest increase will come into effect in January and means that the price of a paid for dinner in a primary school or special school, for instance, will have risen from £2.60 to £3.40 since the start of 2026. Pupils eligible for free school meals will not be affected. The rise in school dinner prices is not the only measure introduced by the EA in response to what they describe as "an exceptionally challenging financial position". There will also be a change to some menus in schools, replacing baked desserts with cheaper alternatives. At Malone Integrated College about 55% of pupils have free school meal entitlement and there are also a lot of parents who are on lower incomes. When the prices of school meals increased earlier this year, Leslie said she remembers "sitting with the head of the cafeteria and heartbreakingly decide how much to put up each item". "I think the cumulative effect of this will be immense, particularly families who have multiple children, both at a primary school and a post-primary school, and trying to make ends meet, it's going to become incredibly difficult," she said. "I firmly believe families are going to struggle at Malone. "I do believe that there will be some families and some young people who will be worried about the stigma attached to this, and won't voice their concerns and won't ask for help. And as an integrated school, that's really sad for us." She added that she thought it would be "quite cutthroat for families". "Already, we have some of our children, particularly in junior school talking about Christmas and how they've had discussions with their families that things are going to be much more scaled down... just with the general cost of living crisis. "This is only going to amplify the situation even more for young people." Leslie added that not having a healthy, balanced diet or going without food will be a "barrier to learning". Why are school dinner prices going up? Education Minister Paul Givan said he was disappointed and concerned but added it was due to underfunding of the education sector as a whole. "I don't want this to be introduced but it is a result of the Education Authority not having sufficient funding," he told the BBC's Good Morning Ulster programme. He said education often bears "the greatest burden" during cost-saving exercises and argued his department should receive a greater share of Stormont's budget. Givan also said the "inadequate" funding that Stormont receives from Westminster was "bearing down on a huge number of public services in Northern Ireland". Stormont ministers are yet to agree a budget, despite weeks of talks with Secretary of State Sir Chris Byrant, who has repeatedly said there is "no more money". Christos Gaitatzis is the principal of Omagh High and described the increase of 15% on a school meal as "excessive". "What is the price index at the moment – is it 3,4, 5%? I would imagine that would be the reasonable increase that you would put on anything, so they are going three times the value - to me it is unreasonable," he told BBC News NI Close to 30% of pupils at his school are on free school meals. "You would expect that the cost for a child every week, when a price of a meal is close to £5, we are talking about £20 a week, £100 a month – that's a significant cost for lunch," Gaitatzis said. "So other measures have to be taken by the families in order to make savings, for example pack lunches – then would that diet be balanced? "We're talking about a society where the importance of nutrition provided by schools has significant impact on your mental and physical health, so you effectively deter these families and children having these nutritious meals by putting the price up. "Clearly this will have an overall future impact on the health of the kids." 'Flabbergasted' Northern Ireland's commissioner for children and young people said he was ''flabbergasted" at the change. Chris Quinn said what makes the move "particularly difficult to accept is that it comes shortly after schools were directed towards energy-saving guidance advising people who were cold to wear more clothes rather than turn up the thermostat". "I strongly advised the Education Authority to remove that guidance and made clear that responsibility for financial pressures in education should not be transferred to children and families." The commissioner added: "Children did not create the financial crisis in education and they should not be expected to pay the price for it. "School meals are not a luxury. For many children they are an essential part of the school day, and these increases will hit hardest those families already struggling with the cost of living." What other costs are increasing? Payments to schools for school milk are at risk. The EA currently pays milk subsidies to about 500 schools. It is to seek funding from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs. The EA is also planning to offer more parents payments to transport their children to school rather than paying for taxis. At present, some parents receive payments if their children are eligible for free school transport but no private providers, like taxis, are available. Charges for EA music lessons for pupils are also set to rise again, and some schemes run in schools will no longer be funded. The authority, however, has not specified what is at risk. 'These were difficult decisions' The EA said it was being asked to deliver important services to young people "with insufficient funding". It said it hoped to save £20m by introducing the measures on top of £30m saved this year. It added that costs, such as providing energy for schools, continued to rise. "These were difficult decisions which sought to balance our commitment to children and young people alongside the requirement to live within the funding allocated for the year." - Published14 January - Published5 November 2025

news.title: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
news.summary: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow have all sent delegations to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
news.summaryTr: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow have all sent delegations to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
news.articleText: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say - Published Trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have begun in Abu Dhabi. Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said yesterday that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. "An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X. Ahead of the meeting, the two US envoys met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials in Abu Dhabi, and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was adamant that France, the UK and Germany "will indeed be in the meeting room". European officials are wary of Russia trying to secure a deal with the US on future "collective security" without them, and Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict are still far apart. A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. Since then, European leaders - who have been largely excluded from peace talks – have pushed to be involved in the process amid concerns that decisions about the security of their continent would be made without them. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged on Monday to include Nato allies and EU members into any "meaningful discussions about Europe's security architecture". President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly stated Kyiv wanted Europe to be part of the talks. The US official said the Americans would propose moving into a multilateral format bringing the Europeans into the discussion. "Hopefully we'll get the Russians on board," the official said, while acknowledging that "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans." Since the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine which "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result into a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believes Trump wants "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Putin start real negotiations is by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi will include Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv is sending several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations." "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believes Trump wants "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Putin start real negotiations is by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi will include Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv is sending several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations." "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." news.summary: The Congolese army's fight against rebel groups has long been hampered by disarray within its ranks.

news.titleTr: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'
news.summaryTr: The Congolese army's fight against rebel groups has long been hampered by disarray within its ranks.
news.articleText: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards' - Published At least 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death in the Democratic Republic of Congo for cowardice, mutiny and refusing to obey orders, local media report. The sentences followed a trial of 71 soldiers before a military court in Walikale, in North Kivu province, in eastern DR Congo. Four soldiers were acquitted, while another was sentenced to 10 years in prison. The army said the trial was intended to improve discipline among troops as they battle armed groups in eastern DR Congo. The region has endured decades of conflict, with fighting continuing between government forces and the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a rebel coalition that includes the M23 group. The soldiers were reportedly arrested on 20 October in Walikale, where they were accused of abandoning their positions and fleeing during clashes with FRN fighters. The Congolese army's campaign against armed groups, including the M23, has long been undermined by poor discipline and disorganisation within its ranks. The government has repeatedly accused neighbouring Rwanda of supporting the M23, an allegation denied by both Kigali and the rebels despite overwhelming evidence. The army has faced persistent criticism over its lack of professionalism and disciplined, while soldiers have complained of poor pay and inadequate equipment. Last month, another 27 soldiers were sentenced to death on similar charges of cowardice after reportedly withdrawing from the frontline during clashes with rebels. In March 2024, DR Congo lifted a 20-year moratorium on the death penalty, citing the need to remove "traitors" within the army. The government said capital punishment would also apply to people involved in armed groups, insurrection, as well as committing treason and war crimes. The decision to reinstate the death penalty was widely criticised by rights groups. However, no formal executions have been carried out since the moratorium was lifted. Since the beginning of 2025, at least 507 soldiers have been convicted, including 381 death sentences, according to figures compiled by French broadcaster RFI. In October 2025, former Congolese President Joseph Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia on charges including war crimes and treason. He denied the accusations, but did not appear in court to defend himself. He has since been named as the FRN's leader. news.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
news.summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.

news.titleTr: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
news.articleText: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy. Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign. "I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Speaking later at a White House press briefing, Trump told reporters, "I know the FBI is looking into" the affair but did not give further details on the investigation, or confirm when it was launched. Trump added he thought that Huang was an "honourable guy and I feel very confident that he will be in good shape" after the investigations. The FBI declined to comment when contacted by the BBC. Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology. The revelations knocked about $250bn (£190bn) off Nvidia's value on Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%. US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang. According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring this year, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published11 hours ago - Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published15 hours ago Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia. Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Nvidia's Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage. Megaspeed's office in Singapore's central business district appeared to be operational and staffed on Tuesday. The BBC was refused entry to its floor, but spoke to a staff member by phone who said they had no comment and directed all queries to the company's PR team. The BBC has emailed Megaspeed several times for comment. Nvidia, co-founded by Jensen Huang, is also a major focus in the AI technology race between the US and China, with officials in Washington treating its exports to Beijing as a matter of national security - a key reason why Huang's affair has sparked concerns. Also on Monday, Huang and Nvidia were sued in a proposed class action lawsuit in California that accuses them of defrauding shareholders by concealing his ties with the suspected Chinese spy. The lawsuit alleges that the company lied to the media about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, "who is suspected of seeking to help smuggle Nvidia products to China." The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment on the lawsuit. 'An honourable guy' At the White House, Trump was asked several times when he was made aware of the relationship. He said he was informed "over a period of time" but was not specific. "I hope there's no problem, I believe he is suffering greatly," the president added. He said he spoke to Huang on the phone on Monday "just to see if he's feeling alright, how you doing and I asked him about that and he said he absolutely had no idea that the person in question was a spy". Trump has raised concerns that allowing China to lead in AI would supercharge Beijing's military and surveillance capabilities. The president added he was "sure" Chinese leader Xi Jinping would "ask me about it" when they next met. Huang has admitted that he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He said on Monday that he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation the company had launched. Huang has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week, however it is unclear whether Huang will appear. A letter said the briefing would be "on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang". Nvidia has declined to comment, while the the BBC has also contacted the committees. - Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond - Published13 hours ago - AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values - Published3 days ago Some workers the BBC spoke to at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters on Monday said it was business as usual, despite the intense attention on the company. Nvidia has been around for decades, with Huang founding it with two other engineers in 1993, but its rise to one of the world's most valuable and powerful companies has only been recent. It originally designed computer chips for gaming, but its decision to shift focus to AI development turned it into the powerhouse it is today. Its chips have become so valuable to the AI buildout that the White House previously imposed controls on where its advanced products could be sold. The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US. But Huang has long been against restricting sales to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology. In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions. Nvidia's most advanced AI semiconductors including the GB200 Blackwell super chip remain blocked from the Chinese market. Additional reporting by Tessa Wong in Singapore - Published16 September - Published14 September

news.summary: Securitize agreed to buy River One to bring stablecoin funding to asset-backed lending and expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

news.titleTr: Securitize agrees to buy River One to expand into asset-backed lending
news.summaryTr: Securitize agreed to buy River One to bring stablecoin funding to asset-backed lending and expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.
news.articleText: Securitize agrees to buy River One to expand into asset-backed lending Securitize agreed to buy River One to bring stablecoin funding to asset-backed lending and expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. BlackRock-backed tokenization platform Securitize agreed to buy River One, a New York financing firm, in a deal that would expand the tokenization company into asset-backed lending, the company said Monday. The deal would add a new financing layer to Securitize’s platform, expanding into asset-backed lending, according to a Monday release. River One is developing technology that would let lenders tap stablecoin funding. Lenders could use pools of small business loans or receivables as collateral to borrow money and fund new loans. The acquisition would give Securitize a role in arranging credit alongside its existing business issuing and servicing tokenized assets for firms such as BlackRock. The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. Securitize ranks as the second-largest real-world asset (RWA) platform with $3.7 billion in total RWA value. Ondo ranks first with $4.1 billion, according to RWA.xyz. Securitize announced the deal alongside Q3 results. Revenue rose 13% from a year earlier to $18.6 million, while the company posted a $66.3 million net loss. Securitize said about $60 million of the loss reflected largely noncash expenses and accounting charges tied mainly to its business combination and public listing. Cointelegraph reached out to Securitize and River One for comment. Related: Securitize falls 16% after earnings miss, tokenization revenue drops

news.title: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India
news.summary: The remains will be taken to Nagaland, where tribal leaders plan a joint memorial and burial.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India
news.summaryTr: The remains will be taken to Nagaland, where tribal leaders plan a joint memorial and burial.
news.articleText: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India - Published The University of Oxford has returned the remains of 39 people taken from the Naga community during British colonial rule in India. A delegation of around 30 people from Nagaland, a mountainous state in north-eastern India, attended a ceremony at Oxford's Pitt Rivers Museum on Monday to mark the handover. The remains, most of which are skulls, will be taken back to India and given what Naga tribal leaders have described as a "respectful rest". There are plans to bury them under a joint memorial in a park in Nagaland. Museum director Laura Van Broekhoven described it as "a historic moment that will be part of stories told to next generations". She said the remains were finally on their way home after overcoming "so much red tape everywhere". The human remains were displayed at the Oxford museum for decades before being removed from public view in 2020 as part of what it described as a "decolonisation process". The Pitt Rivers Museum holds more than 6,000 objects associated with Naga culture, believed to be the largest such collection in the world. Most were acquired during British colonial rule in India and Myanmar (the former Burma). The museum's website lists 219 items as human remains. These were added to the museum's collection between 1910 and 1940 and mostly collected by two colonial administrators who were anthropologists. The museum's website, external mentions that the objects collected during this period were "frequently confiscated during punitive military expeditions, rather than freely given". During their visit to Oxford, the Naga delegation also met descendants of one of the anthropologists involved in collecting the remains. "The manner in which these human remains were taken away from our land leaves much for us to speculate," one of the tribal leaders, Thejao Vihienuo, told AFP. "I suspect that nobody would have given the skull of his father or his grandfather as a gift to another person." Anthropologists say that the Naga people once practised head hunting, severing the heads of enemies as trophies. But they also kept the heads of their own chiefs at the centre of villages. The Pitt Rivers Museum, founded in the 19th Century, has previously returned human remains to indigenous communities in Australia, New Zealand and the US. The latest handover to India concerns only the 39 ancestral remains and comes after a visit by a Naga delegation to Oxford in 2025, when it formally requested their return. The museum had announced in September that the remains would be returned to India.

news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds and European regulators sought industry participants to help establish common standards for tokenized securities. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain. EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities. Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers. The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets. The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards. In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money.

news.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-
